newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to open bids for two B Band areas Friday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to open bids for two B Band areas Friday.

text.p: Brazil will open bids Friday for two B Band cellular concessions, one covering Sao Paulo state outside the metropolitan area, and the other comprising six northeastern states, the Communications Ministry said.
"On Friday, we will be opening the envelopes for Areas Two and 10," said Francisco Mendonca, chief spokesman for the ministry.

The areas will be the fourth and fifth B Band licenses awarded in the on-going opening of Brazil's promising cellular telephone sector. The government has set base prices of 600 million reais for Area Two and 230 million reais for Area 10.
So far, contracts have been granted for three of the 10 B Band concessions, including one for the coveted Area One concession covering metropolitan Sao Paulo area.
The government also has awarded the contracts for Area Seven, including Brasilia and much of central-western Brazil, and Area Nine, comprised of the northeastern states of Bahia and Sergipe.

Mendonca said the BCP S.A. consortium, including BellSouth Corp, which won the Area One license, and the Vicunha Telecomunicacoes S.A. group, winner of Area Nine, were slated to pay their license fees Wednesday.
On July 9, BCP group won Area One with a staggering 2.647 billion-real ($2.45 billion) bid. The Vicunha group snapped up Area Nine with an offer of 250 million reais, 8.7 percent above the base price

Area Seven was awarded in June to Americel S.A., led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada and Telesystem, also of Canada, the lone bidder with an offer of 338.5 million reais, some 25.4 percent above the minimum price.
Americel's concession area includes the largely rural states of Acre, Goias, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Rondonia and Tocantins, and the federal district of Brasilia.

The government received bids in early April for all but one of the 10 concession areas. It is expected to hold a new auction for Area Eight, comprised of the Amazonian states of Amazonas, Roraima, Amapa, Para and Maranhao, once the other licenses are awarded.
